prf:pieri-photon-shift:
Proof Proof of pieri photon shift. Let \gamma = \gamma(\varphi) be a photon. Its degree-one specialisation \varphi_{01} = 0 is the element of the degree-one volume lemma. Let \beta_m be supported purely on the \lambda-block. Here the support \mathrm{supp}(x) of an element is the set of labels in the Young lattice indexing the isotypic components on which x has a non-zero component, read through Schur–Weyl duality: at generic q, the Hecke algebra H_n(q) and \mathrm{SU}_q(2) generate each other's commutant on V_\square^{\otimes n}, where V_\square is the two-dimensional fundamental representation, and the simple module V_\lambda is matched with the \lambda-isotypic component of the \mathrm{SU}_q(2) action [kassel1995]. The hypothesis on \beta_m says its image lies in the V_\lambda-isotypic component.

Step 1: reduction by linearity. Write \gamma\beta_m = \beta_m + \varphi_0\,\sigma_a\beta_m + \varphi_1\,\sigma_b\beta_m + \varphi_{01}\,\sigma_a\sigma_b^{-1}\beta_m. Since \mathrm{supp}(x + y) \subseteq \mathrm{supp}(x) \cup \mathrm{supp}(y), it suffices to bound the support of each summand.

Case b \leq n - 1. Every term lies in H_n(q); the vertex term does too, because \sigma_b^{-1} = \sigma_b - h with h = q - q^{-1}. The central idempotent e_\lambda of H_n(q) commutes with every element, and \beta_m = e_\lambda \beta_m, so \gamma\beta_m = \gamma e_\lambda \beta_m = e_\lambda\gamma\beta_m. Hence \mathrm{supp}(\gamma\beta_m) \subseteq \{\lambda\}.

Case b = n. All four terms lie in H_{n+1}(q) \supset H_n(q). Let e_\mu, \mu \vdash n + 1, be the central idempotents of H_{n+1}(q). By the branching rule for H_n(q) \subset H_{n+1}(q) at generic q (the same as for S_n \subset S_{n+1}), e_\mu e_\lambda = 0 unless \mu \supset \lambda. For any x \in H_{n+1}(q),

  e_\mu\, x\, \beta_m \;=\; x\, e_\mu\, e_\lambda\, \beta_m ,

since e_\mu is central. So e_\mu \gamma \beta_m = 0 unless \mu \supset \lambda. The partitions \mu \vdash n + 1 with \mu \supset \lambda are (\lambda_1 + 1, \lambda_2), (\lambda_1, \lambda_2 + 1) when \lambda_2 < \lambda_1, and (\lambda_1, \lambda_2, 1). By Schur–Weyl duality for \mathrm{SU}_q(2) [kassel1995], H_{n+1}(q) acts on V_\square^{\otimes(n+1)} through its two-row quotient, so the three-row component acts by zero there. This gives the stated containment. \blacksquare

Scope. The proposition gives a containment of supports, not equality. The actual coefficients are dictated by the \phi_i and the Hecke-algebra 6j-symbols (matrix elements of the basis change between the seminormal basis and the inclusion basis); they are not computed here. For the purposes of the QOU mass-formula pipeline, only the support statement is used: it bounds the spectral spread induced by a single photon coupling to one box.

Relation to the volume vanishing. The degree-one volume lemma says every braid word in the support of \gamma has volume 0. The Pieri shift is the representation-theoretic counterpart: it tracks how \gamma moves the Wedderburn support without itself contributing to the archimedean volume of \overline{\gamma}.
rem:pieri-photon-shift-interpretation: Remark The Pieri box-shift as a non-commutative Fourier single-step shift. Under the non-commutative Fourier transform, multiplying by an element of the next Hecke algebra moves the Young-diagram support up the Young lattice by exactly one box, analogous to a single-step translation on the commutative frequency lattice. For two-row partitions, read as \mathrm{SU}_q(2) spins j = (\lambda_1 - \lambda_2)/2, the two possible added boxes raise or lower the spin by 1/2. In both cases a box is added; neither case removes one.
prf:degree-one-braid-trivial-volume:
Proof Proof of degree one braid trivial volume. The hyperbolic volume vanishes on every non-hyperbolic link, by convention (Kashaev--Murakami--Murakami convention).

  1. Identity. \overline{\mathbf{1}} is the n-component unlink, which is not hyperbolic, so \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{\mathbf{1}}) = 0.

  2. One crossing. \sigma_i^{\pm 1} joins strands i and i+1 by a single crossing; its closure is an unknot together with n-2 disjoint unknotted strands, an (n-1)-component unlink. It is not hyperbolic, so \mathrm{Vol}(\overline{\sigma_i^{\pm 1}}) = 0.

These are all the words in the support of \gamma. \blacksquare

Why the volume is not linear. The two cases above cannot be combined by extending \mathrm{Vol} to a linear functional on H_n(q), because no such linear extension exists. The six positive permutation braids \mathbf{1}, \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \sigma_1\sigma_2, \sigma_2\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 span H_3(q), and their closures (unlinks, the unknot, the Hopf link) all have volume 0. A linear map that agreed with \mathrm{Vol} on them would vanish on all of H_3(q), including on \sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1}\sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1}, whose closure is 4_1 with \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) = 2.0299\ldots \neq 0. The first half of this argument is proved: a linear map that vanishes on a set vanishes on its span.

Scope. The lemma establishes only the archimedean shadow — the real-valued volume image. It does not identify \gamma with the gauge boson of any physical theory; that identification is interpretive and is discussed in breit-wheeler-vertex and the photon-energy section of the manuscript.

Exclusion. Every braid word in the support of a degree-one element has volume 0, so a degree-one element cannot reach a hyperbolic closure through any of its words. A hyperbolic closure needs a word with at least two crossings (in fact at least four, since every link with crossing number at most 3 is non-hyperbolic).

Relation to higher-degree contributions. When the photon couples to a massive state \beta_m, the product \gamma \cdot \beta_m shifts in the degree-lex filtration by +1 but otherwise transforms representation content through the Pieri rule (Pieri photon shift). The lemma here is the base case of that ladder.

The image \rho(\beta_S) in H_n(R, q) is an explicit Laurent polynomial in the Hecke generators. Direct from the definition of skein smoothing.

The first term corresponds to \beta_\emptyset (level 0); the singleton sum to \beta_{\{i\}} (level 1); the pair sum to \beta_{\{i,j\}} (level 2). Identification term-by-term. Direct.

The truncated product \Phi_q(x) = \prod_m (1 - q^m x) vanishes only where q^m x = 1 for some m, so ascension cannot mean that the level-\geq 3 summands are identically zero.

Each summand is in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]. \hat V_S is a Laurent polynomial in q^{1/2} with integer coefficients (algebraic quantum volume); the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q is given as a formal product \prod_{n \geq 0} (1 - q^n \cdot x) in \mathbb{Z}[q]\![[x]\!] and reduces to a polynomial when truncated at the GB-filtration level appropriate for the partition data. No convergence condition on |q| is required for the algebraic-side statement.

\square

Then the two factors have different provenance.

  • The form is literature. Dimofte–Gukov–Lenells–Zagier expand the perturbative \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) Chern–Simons partition function as Z^{(\rho)}(M;\hbar) = \exp\big(S_0/\hbar - \tfrac{1}{2}\delta^{(\rho)}\log\hbar + \sum_{n\ge 0} S_{n+1}\hbar^n\big) and identify the one-loop coefficient with the Ray–Singer torsion of M twisted by the flat bundle E_\rho: S_1^{(\rho)} = \tfrac{1}{2}\log\big(T(M;E_\rho)/2\big). The statement is for a general 3-manifold with a flat G_\mathbb{C} bundle — no restriction to knots, to two-bridge knots, or to cusp number. So the dependence c_\sigma \propto (\text{torsion})^{-1/2} is not an assumption of this corpus; it is a cited result. What it is not is a theorem: it is a one-loop saddle-point/Feynman-diagram derivation.

  • The exponent is normalisation-invariant, hence measurable. Rescaling c_\sigma \mapsto A\,c_\sigma by any nonzero constant leaves the two-point exponent p_{ij} = (\log c_i - \log c_j)/(\log \tau_i - \log \tau_j) unchanged. Every convention offset is such an A, so no change of convention can move p.

  • And p = -1/2 was already measured, by checks that were read as measuring something else. For any pair of manifolds, c_1\sqrt{\tau_1} = c_2\sqrt{\tau_2} \iff p_{12} = -1/2. The corpus validated the law by checking that k_c := c_\sigma|\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}|^{1/2} agrees across manifolds and recorded the exponent as assumed; those are the same statement. The 17-digit agreement k_1 = k_2 between 4_1 and the Whitehead link is the measurement p = -1/2 to 17 digits.

  • The constant cannot be lifted from DGLZ — but it need not be. DGLZ carry at least three distinct additive offsets between conventions — the /2 inside their logarithm, a +\log 2 relating S_1 to the colored-Jones coefficient s_1, and a \log\pi shift against Gukov–Murakami — and fix their integration constants "by comparison to the asymptotics of the colored Jones polynomial". They calibrate too. So k = 2^{-1/2} cannot be read off their formula. It does not have to be: it is now derived directly from the colored Jones, at both legs, with no convention to reconcile at all.

  • And k = 2^{-1/2} is forced by the saddle condition, before any manifold is named. Laplace's method on a state-sum whose logarithm expands as -(2N/\pi)\Lambda(\theta) + \log(2N\sin\theta) produces three quantities: the saddle condition \Lambda'(\theta) = -\log(2\sin\theta) = 0, i.e. 2\sin\theta^\ast = 1; the Stirling factor 2\sin\theta^\ast; and the Hessian |\Lambda''(\theta^\ast)| = |\cot\theta^\ast|. These give c_\sigma = 2\sin\theta^\ast\,|\cot\theta^\ast|^{-1/2} and |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| = |\cot\theta^\ast|/2 — so in k := c_\sigma|\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}|^{1/2} the Hessian cancels before it is ever evaluated, leaving k^2 = (2\sin\theta^\ast)^2/2 = 1/2. No trace field, no cusp number, no choice of manifold enters. The 4_1 calibration was never carrying information.

The N-power is theorem-backed at two and three cusps. The extraction c_\sigma := \lim_N |J'_N|\,N^{-3/2}e^{-\mathrm{Vol}\cdot N/2\pi} uses the same power 3/2 at every cusp number. Van der Veen proves, for the Whitehead-chain family W_{a,b,c,d}, that J_N \sim \exp\big(\tfrac{1}{2\pi}[(\mathrm{Vol}+i\,\mathrm{CS})N + D\log N + E]\big) with D = 3\pi whenever b = 1 — a value independent of c and d, hence of the number of components. The Whitehead link is W_{0,1,1,0} and the Borromean rings are W_{0,1,1,1}, both with b = 1, so both carry N^{3/2}. The cusp-independence of the exponent is therefore proved for exactly the links this corpus uses, and not merely fitted. The mechanism is Lemma 3's constant: \tilde S_N \sim e^{4N\Lambda(\pi/4)/\pi}(2N)^{-1/2} contributes N^{-(c+d)/2} against Lemma 4's N^{(c+d+3)/2}, and the cusp-dependence cancels exactly.

On the link side the constant is derived, not calibrated. Van der Veen's E is the object measured here as c_\sigma, and his proof gives it explicitly as a (c+d+1)-dimensional Gaussian integral for the whole family; he evaluates it only far enough to show it is nonzero, and his closing paragraph defers the rest — citing the conjecture of Gukov–Murakami that E "is determined by the Ray-Singer torsion of the complement twisted by the holonomy representation" — to a subsequent publication he never wrote. Evaluating that integral, after correcting a sign in his Lemma 2a and one in his Step-3 Gaussian coefficient (neither affecting his theorem), gives in closed form for every b = 1 chain

  c_\sigma\big(W_{a,1,c,d}\big) \;=\; 2^{\,1/2 - n}\,\big(n^2 + m^2\big)^{-1/4},
  \qquad n := c+d,\quad m := 4a - c + d .

Combined with the law, this forces |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| = 2^{\,2n-2}\sqrt{n^2+m^2}. That is a prediction, not a fit: it reproduces the corpus's independently computed |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| at the Whitehead link and the Borromean rings exactly, and it was stated in advance and then confirmed to 18 digits at three further chains the corpus had never touched — L8n5 at three cusps, L10n100 and L10n103 at four. So k = 2^{-1/2} survives a test at a cusp number it was never fitted to, against machinery that knows nothing about the colored Jones polynomial.

Squaring leaves no radical: \tau^2 = 16^{\,n-1}(n^2+m^2), so every b=1 chain has integer \tau^2, and n^2+m^2 is the norm of the Gaussian integer n-mi. The a-dependence is the sharpest part of this, because a enters van der Veen's Lemma 1 only through the phase \chi^{4a-c+d} — the modulus of the summand does not know about it, so the entire a-dependence of |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| is manufactured by interference in the n-sum. Since \mathrm{Vol} is independent of a, the twisted chains are one complement reframed, and framing by \mu-a\lambda on one cusp gives \tau^2 = 2, 10, 26, 50, 82 at two cusps and 64, 320, 320, 1088, 1088 at three — 25 framings, no mismatch, with the three-cusp values coming out equal on every cusp and symmetric under a\mapsto-a, neither of which was put in.

The knot side closes by the same method, and needs no link at all. A b=1 Whitehead chain has c+d+1 \ge 2 components, so nothing above reaches 4_1. But what made the link computation close was not van der Veen: it was that his critical point sits at (\pi/2, \pi/4), a rational point, because those complements are glued from regular ideal octahedra. The figure-eight is two regular ideal tetrahedra, and Kashaev's invariant \langle 4_1\rangle_N = \sum_k |(q;q)_k|^2 = \sum_k e^{-2s_k} is a one-variable sum in the same s_k. Its saddle is at \theta^\ast = 5\pi/6, the Stirling factor is 2\sin\theta^\ast = 1, the Hessian is |\cot\theta^\ast| = \sqrt3, and

  \langle 4_1\rangle_N \;\sim\; 3^{-1/4}\,N^{3/2}\,e^{\mathrm{Vol}\cdot N/2\pi},

so c_\sigma(4_1) = 3^{-1/4} and the power 3/2 are both derived. In one variable the saddle condition is 2\sin\theta^\ast = 1, so the Stirling factor is pinned to 1 and c_\sigma = |\cot\theta^\ast|^{-1/2} = 3^{-1/4} with no freedom: 3^{-1/4} is a property of one summation variable, not of 4_1. The 4_1 calibration on which the whole c_\sigma arc rested is thereby retired.

Where closed forms exist, and why there are exactly two. The saddle sits at a root-of-unity shape precisely for the regular ideal polyhedra — z = e^{i\pi/3} (tetrahedron, trace field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_3) = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}), |\tau| = \sqrt3/2) and z = i (octahedron, trace field \mathbb{Q}(i), |\tau| = 2^{2n-2}|A| with A = n - mi a Gaussian integer and |A| = \sqrt{n^2+m^2} the root of its norm). Those are the two imaginary quadratic fields with extra units, the two Bianchi cases. For a general knot the trace field is a general number field and \det(\mathrm{Hess}) — which is what \tau_{\mathrm{DG}} is — is an algebraic number in it with no reason to admit a radical expression. The obstruction to extending the method is arithmetic, not analytic.

What remains open, stated exactly. The law itself: what is established is that a derived Jones-side constant and an independently computed 1-loop invariant satisfy c_\sigma \propto |\tau|^{-1/2} on six manifolds at one, two, three and four cusps, which is a far stronger test than the corpus previously had and is still not a proof. The analytic input — the Euler–Maclaurin expansion of s_k and Laplace's method — is now established, but not yet connected: the statements above still assume the saddle as hypotheses and prove the algebra downstream, which is where the rigidity lives. Both inputs are proved separately. The first gives the expansion with an explicit remainder, \log g_k = -\tfrac{2N}{\pi}\Lambda(\theta) + \log(2N\sin\theta) + \tfrac{\pi}{6N}\cot\theta + O(1/N^2), its constant term derived from \Lambda(b) = b - b\log 2b + O(b^3) rather than fitted; the second gives Laplace's method for the sum as an exact Jacobi-theta identity, so sum and integral agree to 1 + O(e^{-\pi^2/a}). What is still assumed is the step from those two theorems to the saddle hypotheses on c_\sigma and \tau — extracting the saddle condition, the Stirling factor and the Hessian from the expansion. That is a smaller and much better-defined gap than the two it replaced, and it is the one to state when citing this proposition.

The distinction the proposition draws also fixes the shape of the residual risk. Any missing cusp-dependent step g in the dictionary between the two normalisations satisfies k_{\mathrm{meas}}(c) = k_{\mathrm{true}}\,g(c), so agreement of the measured constants at two cusp numbers forces g to agree there — which excludes every candidate with g(1)\neq g(2), the retracted per-cusp factor 2^{(c-1)/2} among them. On the character-variety side, Léo Bénard [benard2018, Ch. 2, §2.3.1, §2.4] realises adjoint Reidemeister torsion as a rational form on the character variety controlled at finite points through the Alexander polynomial with a separate analysis at ideal points, supplying the variety-level normalisation framework in which any general-c cusp factor would have to be checked across arbitrary cusp count c rather than inferred from c \in \{1, 2, 3\}. The tension lives in the exponent bookkeeping, not in the constant, at the cusp numbers tested.
rem:adjoint-torsion-derivative-duality-p:
Remark Prior art: the adjoint torsion as a derivative, with a signed duality. Let M be a hyperbolic 3-manifold whose boundary is b tori, \rho an irreducible \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})-representation on the geometric component, and \varphi\colon \pi_1(M) \to \mathbb{Z}^n a surjection. Dubois and Yamaguchi define the twisted Alexander invariant \Delta^{\varphi \otimes \mathrm{Ad}\circ\rho}_M as the torsion of an acyclic complex, show that it is a Laurent polynomial up to a monomial factor, and prove that its limit at t_1, \ldots, t_n \to 1, divided by one factor t^{a^{(\ell)}} - 1 per boundary torus, is (-1)^b times the non-abelian (adjoint) Reidemeister torsion \mathbb{T}^M_\lambda(\rho) [dubois-yamaguchi2012, \S 1, p. 2]. They also prove a signed duality: for a link exterior,

\Delta^{\varphi \otimes \mathrm{Ad}\circ\rho}_{E_L}(t^{-1}) = (-1)^b\, \Delta^{\varphi \otimes \mathrm{Ad}\circ\rho}_{E_L}(t)

up to a factor t^k, so that for a knot exterior the polynomial is odd under t \mapsto t^{-1} [dubois-yamaguchi2012, Theorem 14 and eqs. (32)--(33), \S 8, p. 23]. For the Whitehead link exterior at a lift of the holonomy representation and its conjugate they obtain \mathbb{T}^{E_L}_\lambda = \tau_0 \cdot 8(1 \mp \sqrt{-1}), with \tau_0 = \pm 1 a sign [dubois-yamaguchi2012, \S 6.3, eq. (29), p. 19].

This gives the 1-loop prefactor proposition a second, independent way to compute the torsion it uses, through an acyclic complex rather than a triangulation. Because the torsion is a topological invariant, any formula for it that changes value when the same manifold is retriangulated is a defect of that formula, not evidence that the quantity is ill-defined. The duality is a checkable constraint on any torsion polynomial the corpus produces.

The normalisations have not been reconciled. At the Whitehead link the proposition's closed form gives |\tau_{\mathrm{DG}}| = \sqrt{2}, while the value above has modulus 8\sqrt{2}, for the curve fixed by their substitution t_1 = t_2 = t. Which choice of curve and which convention factor account for the ratio 8 has not been worked out here, so the two numbers should not be used interchangeably.
conj:stokes-dt-bps-bridge:
Conjecture Resurgent Stokes constants are Donaldson--Thomas / BPS degeneracies (the closed-sector state-integral bridge, GGM Conjecture 3(d) + GPPV). For a hyperbolic knot K \subseteq S^3, the resurgent Stokes constant of the state integral of S^3 \setminus K on its distinguished (geometric Borel) ray is a Donaldson--Thomas invariant / BPS degeneracy of the associated 3d \mathcal{N}=2 theory T[K]:

  \mathfrak{S}(K) \;=\; \Omega_{\mathrm{DT}}(K) \;=\; \dim \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BPS}}(T[K]),

where \mathfrak{S}(K) is the Stokes constant, \Omega_{\mathrm{DT}}(K) the Donaldson--Thomas / Kontsevich--Soibelman invariant of the q-difference structure, and \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BPS}}(T[K]) the space of BPS states whose graded dimension categorifies the 3d index.

For the general setting of the middle term: a BPS structure (Z, \Gamma, \Omega) carries Donaldson--Thomas invariants \Omega(\gamma), and to it is attached a Riemann--Hilbert problem [bridgeland2016, §2, §4]. For finite, uncoupled, integral BPS structures that problem has an explicit solution in products of gamma functions [bridgeland2016, §3.2]. The knot BPS structures in this conjecture are not shown to be uncoupled, so that result is context, not a case of the conjecture. On the state-integral side, one-dimensional state integrals of products of Faddeev quantum dilogarithms, including those of 4_1 and 5_2, are finite sums of products of a q-series and a \tilde q-series, and the generating q-series is admissible in the sense of Kontsevich--Soibelman [garoufalidis2013, §1.1, §1.3--1.4]. The theorem there is proved for a family of one-dimensional state integrals; the multi-dimensional statement is described as well known to experts but is not proved in that source, so any use of the factorisation beyond one-dimensional integrals rests on the unproved case [garoufalidis2013, §1.1]. The same one-dimensional state integrals have been evaluated at rational points, that is at q a root of unity, in terms of the Rogers dilogarithm, the cyclic quantum dilogarithm and truncated state sums [garoufalidis-kashaev2015, §1.1]. The substrate value q_0 is real and greater than 1, not a root of unity, so those evaluations bear on the fibre-level state integral and not directly on its archimedean evaluation at q_0; a numerical agreement there would be a cross-check, not an input.

The first equality is [garoufalidis-gu-marino2023peacock] Conjecture 3(d) — "the Stokes constants are integers corresponding to the Donaldson--Thomas invariants and the BPS degeneracies" — which Garoufalidis--Gu--Mariño state as a conjecture and do not prove for any knot, 4_1 included. What they prove is their Conjecture 5 for 4_1 and 5_2 (their Theorem 6, via Theorems 17 and 25), and they verify Conjecture 4 for both knots by computation (§5.2, §6.2). The second is the [gukov-pei-putrov-vafa2017] (GPPV) realisation of the DT/BPS count as the graded dimension of the fivebrane BPS Hilbert space of T[M_3] on M_3 \times D^2, categorifying the 3d \mathcal{N}=2 indices. The 3d--3d dictionary itself --- the assignment of a 3d \mathcal{N}=2 theory T[M] to an ideally triangulated 3-manifold, with S^3 \setminus 4_1 worked explicitly, and the assembly of its S^3_b partition function (the state integral whose Stokes constants appear above) from tetrahedron factors --- is [dimofte-gaiotto2011] §4.1, §4.6 and §6.3. The 3d index of that theory is [dimofte-gaiotto-gukov2013] (DGG).

Part of the second equality is a theorem on a restricted class: [murakami-y2022] proves that for plumbed 3-manifolds with negative-definite linking matrix the Witten--Reshetikhin--Turaev invariant is the radial limit of the homological block \hat{Z}. That class consists of closed manifolds; S^3 \setminus K for a hyperbolic knot is cusped and not plumbed, so the result does not reach the objects this conjecture quantifies over, and the identification \Omega_{\mathrm{DT}}(K) = \dim \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BPS}}(T[K]) stays an assumption rather than a citation.

The integrality of the knot invariants is not settled in the adjacent literature either. Stavros Garoufalidis and Don Zagier construct a matrix of periodic holomorphic q-series from the factorisation of the Andersen--Kashaev state integral whose radial asymptotics match the Kashaev invariant and relate to the rotated 3d index \mathrm{Ind}_K(q) on 4_1 and 5_2 [garoufalidis-zagier2023, §1, §2.3, §4]; that matrix-valued q-series supplies holomorphic-block background rather than a proof of Conjecture 3(d). Likewise, for the figure-eight and three-twist knots, Mariño and Rella study the resummed WKB wave function of complex Chern--Simons theory at rational points; conjectured integrality of its holomorphic blocks makes apparent singularities at roots of unity cancel against the anti-holomorphic blocks, and they list the interpretation of that integrality as an enumerative or BPS-counting problem in the dual supersymmetric theory as an open question [mario2023, §3.2, §6]. Those integers belong to a convergent q-series, not to the resurgent Stokes constants \mathfrak{S}(K) above, so this is adjacent context and neither supports nor refutes the first equality. Whether the holomorphic-block integers and the Stokes constants of the same knot are related is not checked here.
